title: Webflow foundations: structure, classes and responsive layout

say: Webflow foundations: structure, classes and responsive layout.
This is the video for module 1 of Webflow Development.

In Webflow you design visually, but the result is real HTML, CSS and JavaScript. When you add padding, Webflow writes the CSS rule. So you must understand the building blocks. You work in the Designer, on a laptop.

panel.heading: Three parts you will use every day

cards.d: Visual workspace in a desktop browser. It writes real HTML and CSS. Plan to work on a laptop.
Collections for repeating content, like blog posts or team members. Clients add items safely.
Free staging on webflow.io. A real domain needs a paid Site plan.

say: The CMS holds Collections, for content that repeats in the same shape, such as blog posts. Clients can add items without touching your design.

say: Webflow charges two ways. A Workspace plan is for you, the builder. A Site plan is for each live website. Usually the client pays their own Site plan, so the website is legally and financially theirs.

panel.heading: Plans and dollar billing
items: Workspace plan for you; Site plan for each site
Client pays their own Site plan
Check webflow.com/pricing the day you quote
Confirm a card that can pay in dollars
Never pay client hosting without a written deal

say: Prices are in US dollars and change, so check the pricing page on the day you quote. Many Nigerian bank cards limit foreign spending, so confirm a card that can pay before you promise a launch date.
And never pay a client's hosting with your own card without a written agreement on repayment.

say: Every element is a box with four layers: the content, then padding inside the edge, then the border, then margin outside, pushing other boxes away.

panel.heading: Why Tolu's cards did not fit
items: Every box: content, padding, border, margin
Three cards, two 20px gaps: 1,090px. Too wide!

say: For example, Tolu sets a service card 300px wide, with 24px padding each side and a 1px border.

panel.heading: Why Tolu's cards did not fit
items: Every box: content, padding, border, margin
Three cards, two 20px gaps: 1,090px. Too wide!

say: With content-box sizing, width means content only. So each card is really 350px.

panel.heading: Why Tolu's cards did not fit
items: Every box: content, padding, border, margin
Three cards, two 20px gaps: 1,090px. Too wide!

say: Three cards and two 20px gaps make 1,090px. That overflows her 960px container.

panel.heading: Why Tolu's cards did not fit
items: Every box: content, padding, border, margin

say: Webflow's default is border-box, where width includes padding and border. Then the row is 940px and fits. An old code embed had changed it. She removed it, and the row fits.

panel.rule: Border-box: width includes padding and border. 940px fits in 960px.

say: Style with classes, reusable named styles. A combo class, like button plus is-secondary, adds a variation. And name things by meaning. Div Block 47 tells nobody anything.

say: Use Flexbox for a line of things, like a navigation bar or a row of buttons.
Use Grid when you need rows and columns together, like a three-column services area. Columns are sized in fr, a fraction of the free space.
Most visitors arrive on a phone. In Webflow you design on Desktop, and styles cascade down to smaller screens.

panel.heading: Zainab's services grid, desktop to phone
items: Test at 360px and on a real Android phone

panel.heading: Zainab's services grid, desktop to phone

say: Then she previews at 360px and finds a heading overflowing, so she lowers it on Mobile portrait only. Four overrides, not four separate layouts. And always open the link on a real phone.

panel.rule: Set styles on Desktop. Override only what must change below.

say: To remember. Ask about payments and editing needs first. Know your box model. Keep a clean structure with meaningful class names. And design on Desktop, override only what must change, and check every section on a real phone.
